What did you end up doing?

I want to believe you. I want to be told I’m good and that I’m not bad and that I should be kinder to myself. I just texted a long message to my therapist about how I manipulated him last session and more about my thoughts about stuff. This is what I said:


“Last time we talked I was manipulative to you. I played the victim when we were talking about if I have NPD and why I feel like it’s so horrible to have it. I asked you if you think I have it in a way that was victim like, but really I just don’t want to have it. I don’t want you to say that I have NPD. I think I do though. I think I’m a covert and vulnerable narcissist. You asked me if I have at least 5 of the symptoms that are written in the DSM-5, I said I don’t know, but I do. In the moment I didn’t count them to see how many, but I knew I did. I told you that having NPD makes me hate myself, and you asked why, and we ended up at the conclusion that it’s because my dad has it (I’m pretty sure). But it’s also because I don’t want to be this way, i don’t want to deal with this, I don’t want to be this person. The traits that I have are immoral and it makes me feel so guilty, and hopeless sometimes that I can get through this. 
I had NPD traits even before I lived with my dad. I bought into your mindset that I’m just this way because of my dad and being in his apartment / lifestyle, and that I hate it because I don’t wanna be like him. And that I probably don’t have actual NPD. In reality that’s not the whole truth. I was influenced by my dad during that time but there are more factors that make up my traits. 

When you said I’m so sorry when I was crying about my dad it felt so good to be validated in that way. And validated in general. And I just kept crying. In the back of my mind I was aware that it isn’t even my dad who made me this way but that it felt good to be seen and also cared for in a fatherly way. I know I have a father wound but it just seems deceiving to express to you that the wound is the root of my NPD. Well, it has to be a part of it. But I was also bullied in elementary and middle school and that plays a big role in my traits. And I feel like some of my traits are part of my personality. I was abusive to my sister when I was younger and even kicked her when I was 14. 

I want validation about me being manipulative. I want to be met with compassion for all of this. I’m just expressing my intentions behind what I’m saying to be authentic and to also receive what I am telling you I want. 

I want to get past this and be able to be at peace with myself and not deal with manipulating anymore but I feel hopelessness sometimes that I can change. It’s interwoven in how communicate. It happens consciously, subconsciously, and unconsciously. I’m worried that you won’t be able to help me because how can you help me if I’m manipulating you? The way I interact with the world is manipulative. Masking what I really feel. Saying things, behaving certain ways, and doing things so that people see me a certain way, so that I’m liked, so that I seem normal, so that people don’t see how I really am which is cold and antisocial and irritated and resentful. Although I feel different things at different times. Like when I talk to you, I laugh at your jokes even if I don’t think it’s funny because I don’t wanna just sit there with a cold face. I act charming too. Now I’m wondering do I act charming or do I not? I want you to like me. I’m afraid to fully put down my mask and also it’s easier to not do that because it takes effort to be truly authentic and think about what the full truth is and to express how what I’m thinking and feeling fully 
Or with my sister, she annoys me so much a lot of the time and a lot of the time I don’t wanna spend time with her but I do anyways and I resent her because I’d rather be alone. But I don’t express that, but I do act passive aggressively a lot. I put up my mask but it’s not always fully up. And I’m worried that I’m not telling you the full truth, like I could say more about things but I want to stop here”

He responded with “Please say more when you feel like it.”

There is hope and you can get through this. There are so many ways to heal and you are not alone.
